newsitem.title: USA: Firm allegedly gave Medicare false data - report.
newsitem.headline: Firm allegedly gave Medicare false data - report.

text.p: A probe of the Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp. has found evidence that some hospital executives responsible for obtaining reimbursement from Medicare submitted false information, The New York Times said Friday.

The paper cited people with knowledge of the investigation who said the first indictments based on this evidence were expected to come as early as a few months from now in Florida. The indictments would charge that the executives helped submit reports to the government that inflated hospital costs.
Such cost reports are used to calculate federal payments that bring hundreds of millions of dollars to Columbia every year, the paper said.
The charges would be the first indictments in the Columbia investigation, it said.
Earlier in the week, the FBI said it executed search warrants on Columbia sites in six states.
